evidence: crates/susi-core/src/capability_bus.rs (T-DEEPSEEK-95) built the typed CapabilityBus (discovery, permission/timeout/cost enforcement) but it had no production caller: CapabilityRegistry::typed_bus() was reachable only from its own tests (crates/susi-core/src/tests/capability_bus.rs, tests/capability_bus.rs). Fixed (T-INTELLIBITZWT20261005035445-2): crates/susi-core/src/registry.rs adds CapabilityRegistry::dispatch_capability, a real caller that resolves a descriptor from the live typed_bus() snapshot and invokes the actually-registered tool (already MAC-enforced and evidence-captured by register_tool) through the bus's permission/timeout/cost contract. Exposed on 'susi os capabilities' (discover the live global registry's A2A/MCP/HTTP/adapter catalog) and 'susi os capabilities invoke <id> --subject --permission --args --timeout-ms --budget-micros' (dispatch). Verified by tests/capability_bus.rs vc_202_012_mastery: a real Tool is registered on a fresh CapabilityRegistry, discovered through typed_bus(), and dispatched end to end with a passing invocation, a permission denial, a zero-timeout refusal, and an unknown-id refusal, all through dispatch_capability — not a synthetic in-memory catalog. Manually smoke-tested through the built 'susi' binary (discover lists 263 real registered agent/tool/provider capabilities; invoke on an unregistered id returns UnknownCapability cleanly).
missing: Only the Mcp (tool) surface can be dispatched today — A2a (agent) and Adapter (provider) capabilities discover through typed_bus() but dispatch_capability refuses them with InvalidDescriptor, since AgentCapability/Provider have different invocation signatures than Tool::execute and bridging them is unscoped work. HTTP capabilities are registered as Adapter-surfaced providers today (no distinct Http registration path), so the bus's own Http surface has no registry-backed discovery source either, only the synthetic fixture in the bus's own tests. cost_micros is hardcoded to 0 for every typed_bus() descriptor and dispatch outcome — there is still no real per-capability cost model, so budget enforcement is exercised (zero vs non-zero ceilings) but not meaningfully attributed yet.
